angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 520,211 km at 183.15 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.4600 +/- 0.0098 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 183.15 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.747752 solar radii from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-3896 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract): 520,211 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.863 (0.823 to 0.903) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5110.91 K from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3896 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3896 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-3896.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.627, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
